evaluations.verdict: GET non-existent task returns 200 with dummy data instead of 404
evaluations.resoning: When a task is not found, the endpoint returns a fake TaskResponse object with id=0 and empty fields. Requirements state a 404 should be returned.

evaluations.verdict: DELETE /tasks returns 200 with body instead of required 204
evaluations.resoning: The delete_task endpoint returns status_code=200 with a TaskResponse body. Requirements state delete should return 204 No Content.

evaluations.verdict: Missing database error handling in create_task
evaluations.resoning: The create_task function has no try/except around db.add, db.commit, or db.refresh. A DB error will cause an unhandled 500 with no rollback.

evaluations.verdict: Missing database error handling in update_task
evaluations.resoning: The update_task function has no try/except around db.commit or db.refresh. A DB error will cause an unhandled 500 with no rollback.

evaluations.verdict: Missing database error handling in delete_task
evaluations.resoning: The delete_task function has no try/except around db.delete or db.commit. A DB error will cause an unhandled 500 with no rollback.

evaluations.verdict: Unnecessary manual construction of TaskResponse in delete_task
evaluations.resoning: delete_task manually builds a TaskResponse before deleting. This adds boilerplate and is also incorrect since 204 should return no body.

evaluations.verdict: get_tasks returns all tasks with no pagination or limit
evaluations.resoning: Fetching all tasks with db.query(Task).all() with no limit can cause performance and memory issues as the dataset grows.

evaluations.verdict: get_tasks does not filter tasks by owner or user context
evaluations.resoning: All authenticated users can retrieve all tasks. There is no user-scoping, which may expose other users data.
